Medical History

- Current health issues and chronic disease risk factors (e.g., hypertension, diabetes): New onset severe unilateral throbbing headache (>24 hours), photophobia; no prior headache history; no hypertension or diabetes documented; on combined oral contraceptive pill for 6 years; allergy to aspirin.  
- Family history of chronic conditions (e.g., CVD, diabetes): Mother with hypertension and migraine history.  
- Current medications including OTC and traditional medicines: Microgynon (combined oral contraceptive pill), paracetamol taken for headache, no other medications documented; aspirin allergy reported (causes nausea).  
- Immunisation status reviewed (flu, COVID-19, pneumococcal, shingles, tetanus): Not recorded.  
- Sexual/reproductive health status and risks: On combined oral contraceptive pill (Microgynon) for 6 years; no pregnancy; last menstrual period approximately one week ago; no menstrual cycle association with headache noted.  
- Lifestyle: physical activity, diet, tobacco, alcohol, substance use: Occasional alcohol on weekends; non-smoker; no recreational drugs; diet and hydration reportedly normal; no specific physical activity details recorded.  
- Hearing and vision concerns: No visual disturbances; no hearing concerns reported.  
- Mood, mental health, and risk assessment (depression, anxiety, self-harm): Not recorded.  
- Social context: family support, caregiving, housing, financial stressors: Lives with housemates (friends); no other social details documented.

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Clinical presentation is of a new, severe, unilateral (left-sided), throbbing headache with photophobia and no neurological deficits or systemic symptoms.  
- Family history includes migraine and hypertension; personal history negative for prior headaches or chronic medical conditions.  
- Patient is on combined oral contraceptive, a known risk factor for cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST).  
- Working diagnosis: Migraine – supported by headache character, photophobia, family history, absence of focal neurological signs, and improvement with lying down; despite no prior migraine history, typical presentation favors migraine (DDx likelihood: High).  
- Considerations: Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST) due to contraceptive use and headache presentation (DDx likelihood: Medium); no focal neurological signs seen but early CVST may present similarly. Meningitis and brain tumor are low likelihood based on absence of fever, systemic symptoms, and neurological findings.  
- Plan includes symptomatic treatment with paracetamol and initiation of anti-inflammatory medication (e.g., ibuprofen) if tolerated (not aspirin due to allergy), hydration, monitoring for worsening symptoms, and advice to seek urgent care if headache worsens, fever develops, or neurological symptoms arise. Blood pressure check recommended. Temperature monitoring advised with a home thermometer.  
- Referral or further investigations not immediately indicated unless progression occurs.

Health Promotion & Planning

- Education on headache management and warning signs provided, including hydration and avoidance of triggers.  
- Patient advised to monitor blood pressure and temperature at home.  
- No explicit patient health goals or priorities documented.  
- Eligibility for GP Management Plan or Team Care Arrangements: Not recorded.  
- Referrals: not currently indicated; advice to return if symptoms worsen or new symptoms develop.  
- Follow-up: advised to contact clinic if headache persists or worsens; no scheduled recall documented.

Consider

- Mental health support or counselling referral: Not recorded.  
- Specialist referral for complex chronic disease management: Not recorded.  
- Dental referral if oral health issues identified: Not recorded.  
- Optometry referral for visual concerns or regular screening: Not recorded.  
- Audiometry referral if hearing issues suspected: Not recorded.  
- Social work or housing support referral if social determinants affect health: Not recorded.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Migraine: High likelihood; typical presentation with unilateral throbbing headache, photophobia, family history, no neurological deficits.  
- Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST): Medium likelihood; plausible given contraceptive use and new headache, but no neurological signs or systemic symptoms yet.  
- Meningitis: Low likelihood; headache with photophobia but no fever, neck stiffness, or systemic signs make this unlikely.  

Quality checks

- Missing but clinically expected elements: vital signs including BP and temperature; immunization status review; anthropometric data; relevant investigations such as blood tests or imaging to exclude serious causes given contraceptive use.  
- Internal conflicts or contradictions: No major conflicts noted between transcript and DDx findings.  
- Transcript quality notes: Transcript is clear and mostly complete; some patient identifying details partial or omitted.
